---
title: "How do I find what columns and data types are in my dataset?"
---

## What the question asks

How do I find what columns and data types are in my dataset?

## Steps in RStudio

1. Store the table in a data frame.

2. Run names(), str(), head(), and summary().

3. Choose columns based on actual content, not their position alone.

## Runnable example

```{r}
d <- data.frame(site=c("A","B","C"), depth_cm=c(12,19,NA))
print(names(d))
str(d)
print(head(d))
print(summary(d))
```

## Interpret the result

Here site is text and depth_cm is numeric with one missing measurement. Summary reports the available values; the missing row must be handled explicitly.

## Check before applying this to real data

Verify units and possible missing values. Numeric-looking text is not necessarily imported as numeric.
